subject: coloring faceted histograms according to value

messages.author: d7a43f3c8dc40522
messages.subject: coloring faceted histograms according to value
parts:
I have something that I would like to do, but I have no idea if it is
even possible.

I have a set of data that is very similar to the diamonds dataset. I
plot this dataset like this:

ggplot(diamonds,aes(x=carat)) + geom_histogram() + facet_grid(cut~color)

Now, if possible, I would like to change the colors of the histogram.
I would like the color to change
according to a value in the data frame, which in my case would be the
same value per facet. In this
case, lets say it would be the mean of the carat. I would preferably
like it to go from a pale color for low
values to a deeper color for higher values, but any color gradient would do.

I see from the doc it is possible to use palettes to plot color
gradients, so I think this could be done, but
I have trouble seeing how I can apply it.

TIA,

Karin

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: coloring faceted histograms according to value
parts:
hi, try this

d2 <- merge(diamonds, aggregate(carat~color, mean, data=diamonds),
by="color", suffix=c("", ".mean"))
ggplot(d2,aes(x=carat, fill=carat.mean)) + geom_histogram() +
facet_grid(cut~color)

and you can specify the color gradient by scale_fill_continuous etc.
as you want.
